acceptance_criterion.definition: A stable, objectively verifiable condition attached to governed work.

action_intent.definition: A typed proposed mutation containing actor, authority, scope, target, risk, approval, idempotency, and audit identity.

adapter.definition: A stable internal interface that isolates an external provider, tool, host, or storage backend.

admission_control.definition: The deterministic decision that sufficient budget, capacity, policy, and isolation exist before work starts.

artifact.definition: A content-addressed file or byte object produced, consumed, tested, or released by the platform.

assurance_layer.definition: Controls that prevent loops, scope drift, unsupported truth, skipped verification, and false completion.

autonomy_director.definition: The advisory intelligence that interprets goals and recommends plans while deterministic authority commits state.

backpressure.definition: Reduced or stopped admission caused by queue, budget, provider, machine, or verification pressure.

branch_guardian.definition: Repository governance role that protects branch, base, worktree, and work-in-progress integrity.

budget_governor.definition: Authority that accounts for spend and quotas and admits billable work through policy.

budget_pressure.definition: A mode indicating constrained, critical, or exhausted spending and quota capacity.

build_sequencer.definition: Component that turns accepted work and dependencies into an ordered, recomputable build plan.

candidate_complete.definition: A worker claim that implementation is ready for independent completion evaluation, not final done state.

canonical_state.definition: The authoritative deterministic project representation used for decisions and transitions.

capability.definition: A qualified behavior that a worker, model, provider, or tool can supply under known constraints.

capability_registry.definition: The machine-readable catalog of available capabilities, versions, constraints, cost, resources, and qualification state.

circuit_breaker.definition: A bounded failure-state mechanism that suppresses repeated unsafe calls and permits controlled recovery probes.

completion_gate.definition: Deterministic authority that verifies criteria, tests, evidence, review, traceability, blockers, and freshness before done.

conflict_graph.definition: Graph of work items that cannot run together because of shared or incompatible resources.

context_broker.definition: Authority that decides which trusted information a worker may and must receive.

context_compiler.definition: Service that assembles normalized purpose-specific context from authoritative project records.

context_firewall.definition: Policy boundary that prevents unauthorized data, secrets, or instructions from reaching a provider or worker.

context_pack.definition: An immutable, content-addressed, purpose-specific bundle supplied to a delegated worker.

context_receipt.definition: Worker acknowledgement of the context consumed, omissions, conflicts, and additional needs.

control_kernel.definition: Deterministic authority that owns canonical state and admissible transitions.

correlation_id.definition: Identifier shared by events, logs, traces, work, evidence, and actions from one logical operation.

decision_center.definition: Operator surface for inspecting material decisions, inputs, authority, alternatives, and provenance.

delegation_envelope.definition: Structured assignment containing objective, scope, constraints, sources, outputs, authority, and return protocol.

disposition.definition: The explicit accepted, superseded, excluded, rejected, or unresolved treatment of a requirement or candidate.

dynamic_lane.definition: A temporary execution lane derived from eligible work and resources rather than a permanent agent slot.

evidence.definition: Observed output or state linked to a claim, method, environment, time, revision, and digest.

evidence_ledger.definition: Append-only registry of evidence records and supersession history.

fencing_token.definition: Monotonic or unique lease identity used to reject actions from stale owners.

golden_journey.definition: Stable critical end-to-end scenario that must pass for release readiness.

external_precondition.definition: A capability or external condition that remains objectively unavailable after safe autonomous resolution attempts; the autonomy runtime owns deterministic rechecks while unaffected lanes continue.

idempotency_key.definition: Stable operation identity that prevents a retried mutation from duplicating state.

instruction_trust.definition: Authority and trust classification applied to instructions before they may influence action.

jira_steward.definition: Governance role that owns Jira synchronization, hygiene, hierarchy, comments, transitions, and reconciliation.

lease.definition: Time-bounded ownership of a resource with holder, scope, expiry, renewal, release, and fencing identity.

loop_guard.definition: Control that detects repeated ineffective execution and stops or escalates it.

merge_gate.definition: Authority that permits integration only when branch, review, policy, test, and evidence conditions are satisfied.

open_decision.definition: A stable unresolved choice with options, constraints, resolution method, and decision gate.

operator_inbox.definition: Prioritized queue of autonomous incident owners, unavailable capabilities, recheck schedules, impact, and recovery verification.

outbox.definition: Durable queue of intended external mutations awaiting idempotent delivery and reconciliation.

project_profile.definition: Policy bundle that selects services, verification, environments, and constraints for a project class.

provider_state.definition: Explicit runtime health and eligibility state used by routing and recovery.

release_readiness.definition: Evidence-backed determination that applicable release, deployment, operational, security, and recovery conditions are satisfied.

repository_steward.definition: Governance role that owns branch, worktree, pull-request, protection, cleanup, and reconciliation policy.

resource_admission.definition: Decision that requested compute and concurrency resources can be allocated safely.

risk_based_verification.definition: Selection of independent evidence types and test depth according to impact and uncertainty.

rpo.definition: Maximum acceptable loss of durable state measured from the latest recoverable point.

rto.definition: Maximum acceptable time to restore a required capability after failure.

safe_parallel_set.definition: Set of eligible work items whose conflicts are absent, isolated, or protected by leases.

scope_governor.definition: Control that enforces accepted work boundaries, change budgets, and scope-change review.

spend_lease.definition: Bounded authorization for billable or quota-consuming work.

split_brain.definition: Failure in which more than one controller believes it has canonical mutation authority.

stale_evidence.definition: Evidence no longer applicable because source, revision, environment, policy, or dependent state changed.

truth_registry.definition: Registry of material claims and facts with provenance, verification, freshness, and supersession.

verified_fact.definition: A claim accepted under applicable verification, authority, and freshness policy.

verified_outcome_cost.definition: Total cost required to produce an accepted result including retries, context, review, and rework.

work_item.definition: Stable Jira-mirrored unit of governed implementation, verification, investigation, or recovery work.

worktree.definition: Git working directory attached to an isolated branch for conflict-safe parallel work.
